name_zh: 甘地：从殖民顺民到非暴力革命领袖的『萨提亚格拉哈』抗争与自我苦行治理范式
name_en: Gandhi: From Colonial Subject to Nonviolent Revolutionary Leader — the 'Satyagraha' Resistance and Self-Ascetic Governance Paradigm
description_zh: 甘地（Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi，1869-1948）是印度独立运动的非暴力领袖、政治家与精神导师。他在南非经历种族歧视后形成「萨提亚格拉哈（Satyagraha，真理坚持/非暴力抵抗）」理念，返回印度后将其发展为推翻英国殖民统治的核心斗争工具。甘地的核心思维贡献在于将「非暴力」从个人道德修养升维为可操作的集体政治斗争方法论——通过食盐长征、纺织运动（Swadeshi）、种姓消除、宗教和解等具体行动，将道德力量转化为实际的制度变革。他以苦行僧式的自我约束（简朴生活、禁食、手工纺织）作为政治斗争的「道德杠杆」，将个人苦难转化为集体动员的能量。甘地是Protreptic中模式19（非暴力抵抗法）在南亚政治传统中的唯一完整样本，也是模式6（统一战线法）在「跨阶级、跨宗教、跨国界的广泛联盟」场景的独特代表。
description_en: Mahatma Gandhi (Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi, 1869-1948) was India's nonviolent revolutionary leader, politician, and spiritual guide. After experiencing racial discrimination in South Africa, he formed 'Satyagraha' (truth force / nonviolent resistance) philosophy, which he developed into the core struggle tool for overthrowing British colonial rule upon returning to India. Gandhi's core thinking contribution lies in elevating 'nonviolence' from personal moral cultivation to an operable collective political struggle methodology — through Salt March, Swadeshi (self-reliance) movement, caste elimination, and religious reconciliation, transforming moral power into actual institutional change. He used ascetic self-discipline (simple living, fasting, hand-spinning) as 'moral leverage' in political struggle, converting personal suffering into collective mobilization energy. Gandhi is the only complete sample of mode 19 (Nonviolent Resistance) in South Asian political tradition, and the unique representative of mode 6 (United Front) in 'cross-class, cross-religious, transnational broad alliance' scenarios.
reason_zh: 甘地填补了Protreptic在「非暴力革命工程化」领域的南亚空白。他是模式19（非暴力抵抗法）的唯一完整样本，展示了如何将个人道德修养转化为可操作的集体政治斗争工具；也是模式6（统一战线法）在「跨阶级、跨宗教、跨国界广泛联盟」场景的独特代表。他的「苦行僧式道德杠杆」策略为Protreptic提供了「以最低暴力代价实现最高政治变革」的经典案例，对全球民权运动（马丁·路德·金、曼德拉早期理念）产生了深远影响。
reason_en: Gandhi fills Protreptic's South Asian gap in 'nonviolent revolution engineering'. He is the only complete sample of mode 19 (Nonviolent Resistance), demonstrating how personal moral cultivation can be transformed into operable collective political struggle tools; also the unique representative of mode 6 (United Front) in 'cross-class, cross-religious, transnational broad alliance' scenarios. His 'ascetic moral leverage' strategy provides Protreptic with a classic case of 'achieving highest political change at lowest violence cost', profoundly influencing global civil rights movements (Martin Luther King, early Mandela philosophy).
steps_zh: 第1步（模式19非暴力抵抗法）：萨提亚格拉哈原理化——在南非经历种族歧视后，将印度传统中的「不害（Ahimsa）」从宗教戒律转化为政治斗争工具，确立「以真理对抗不义、以自我受苦替代暴力报复」的核心原则
第2步（模式6统一战线法）：跨阶层联盟构建——将印度农民、城市工人、商人、知识分子、妇女、低种姓（不可接触者）和不同宗教群体整合为统一斗争阵线，以「纺织运动」作为物质纽带（每个人纺纱即参与独立），以「不可接触者的权利」作为道德制高点
第3步（模式38摸石头过河）：渐进式制度变革——从局部非暴力不合作（抵制英货、退出政府职位）到全国食盐长征（1930年步行240英里制盐），以具体可操作的象征性行动逐步扩大斗争规模，避免一次性全面对抗
第4步（模式31框架效应法）：殖民合法性重构——通过绝食、手工纺织、简朴生活等苦行僧式自我约束，将「殖民统治的文明优越论」框架翻转，使英国统治的道德成本远超军事成本
第5步（范式固化）：非暴力革命遗产——将「真理坚持→跨阶层联盟→渐进变革→合法性翻转」四环沉淀为可复制的非暴力斗争母板，对全球民权运动产生深远影响
steps_en: Step 1 (Mode 19 Nonviolent Resistance): Satyagraha principle — after racial discrimination in South Africa, transform Indian traditional 'Ahimsa' (non-harm) from religious precept to political struggle tool, establish core principle of 'confronting injustice with truth, substituting self-suffering for violent retaliation'

Step 2 (Mode 6 United Front): Cross-class alliance building — integrate Indian peasants, urban workers, merchants, intellectuals, women, low-caste (untouchables), and diverse religious groups into unified struggle front, using 'spinning movement' as material bond (each person spinning thread = participating in independence) and 'untouchables' rights as moral high ground

Step 3 (Mode 38 Testing Waters): Gradual institutional change — from localized nonviolent non-cooperation (boycott British goods, withdraw government posts) to nationwide Salt March (1930: 240-mile walk to make salt), use concrete operable symbolic actions to gradually expand struggle scale, avoiding one-time comprehensive confrontation

Step 4 (Mode 31 Framing Effect): Colonial legitimacy reconstruction — through fasting, hand-spinning, simple living and other ascetic self-discipline, flip the 'colonial civilization superiority' framework, making Britain's moral cost of rule exceed military cost

Step 5 (Paradigm Solidification): Nonviolent revolution legacy — condense 'Satyagraha→cross-class alliance→gradual change→legitimacy flip' into replicable nonviolent struggle template, profoundly influencing global civil rights movements
expected_zh: 掌握甘地「萨提亚格拉哈」从南非经验到印度全国斗争的发展路径；理解食盐长征、纺织运动、不可接触者权利等具体行动如何构成非暴力斗争的可操作链条；评估甘地苦行僧式道德杠杆对全球民权运动的持续影响。
expected_en: Master Gandhi's 'Satyagraha' development path from South African experience to nationwide Indian struggle; understand how Salt March, spinning movement, untouchables' rights and other specific actions form operable nonviolent struggle chains; evaluate the continuing influence of Gandhi's ascetic moral leverage on global civil rights movements.
case_zh: 1930年食盐长征：甘地带领78名追随者步行240英里至海边制盐，直接挑战英国食盐专卖法。这一看似简单的「违法」行动成为印度独立运动的转折点——数万人参与盐走私，各地发起抵制英货运动。1942年「退出印度」决议要求英国立即撤离，虽遭镇压但动摇了殖民统治根基。甘地晚年致力于印度与巴基斯坦分治后的宗教和解，以绝食阻止德里暴乱。他的「手工纺织（Charkha）」不仅是经济自给符号，更是每个印度人参与独立的物质纽带。甘地非暴力理念直接启发了马丁·路德·金的美国民权运动和曼德拉早期的反种族隔离斗争，成为20世纪全球非暴力政治斗争的母板。
case_en: 1930 Salt March: Gandhi led 78 followers on a 240-mile walk to the sea to make salt, directly challenging British salt monopoly. This seemingly simple 'illegal' action became turning point of Indian independence movement — tens of thousands participated in salt smuggling,各地 launched boycott British goods campaigns. 1942 'Quit India' resolution demanded immediate British withdrawal; though suppressed, it undermined colonial rule foundations. In his final years Gandhi worked on religious reconciliation after India-Pakistan partition, using fasting to stop Delhi riots. His 'hand-spinning (Charkha)' was not just an economic self-reliance symbol but material bond for every Indian participating in independence. Gandhi's nonviolent philosophy directly inspired Martin Luther King's American civil rights movement and Mandela's early anti-apartheid struggle, becoming the template for 20th-century global nonviolent political struggle.
intellectual_tradition: Hindu Asceticism / Satyagraha Philosophy / Colonial Resistance
cross_cultural_impact: Inspired global civil rights movements (MLK, early Mandela); Satyagraha became universal framework for nonviolent political struggle; influenced UN decolonization discourse
